newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire troops loot as rebels approach diamond town.
newsitem.headline: Zaire troops loot as rebels approach diamond town.

text.p: Zairean soldiers looted vehicles from Zaire's diamond mining capital Mbuji-Mayi on Friday, sources in the town said.

Troops had stolen vehicles from the state-owned La Miniere de Bakwanga (MIBA) diamond mining company and were fleeing towards the town of Kananga, about 100 km (62 miles) to the west, expatriate sources said.
They also said rebels were believed to be in villages on the outskirts of Mbuji-Mayi in diamond-rich Kasai province, but that there were no confirmed sightings of rebel fighters in the city itself.

Sources from Zaire's Gecamines mining company in Lubumbashi said that a column of rebels took the town of Luena, 300 km (186 miles) northwest of Lubumbashi on Friday morning and were heading southwards.
There had been little if any fighting in Luena and youths in the area were rallying to the side of the rebels, who were apparently heading for Lubumbashi.
The MIBA mine, 20 percent owned by Belgium company Sibeka, produced around 6.5 million carats of diamonds in 1996.
